chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Words of God, Mighty and Majestic,
'And I breathed into him from My Spirit' —

how was this blowing? So he said: 'The Spirit (Ruh) moves like the wind (Reeh), and it was named Ruh because it derived its name from Reeh (wind). He differentiated it from the term Reeh because the spirits are of the genus of the wind. And He attributed it to His Own Self because He chose it above the rest of the spirits — just as He said for a house among houses: "My house," and for a messenger among the messengers: "My Friend (Khalil)," and the likes of that. And all of that is created, made, newly-originated, nourished, and regulated.'

key_terms.اصْطَفَاهُ: Istafa — He chose/selected it; the reason for attributing the spirit to God (honor, not essence)
key_terms.الرُّوح: Ruh — the Spirit; a created entity distinct from the divine essence
key_terms.الرِّيح: Reeh — wind; the etymological root from which 'Ruh' is derived
key_terms.خَلِيلِي: Khalili — My Friend (Intimate Friend); referring to the title of Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
key_terms.مَخْلُوقٌ مَصْنُوعٌ مُحْدَثٌ مَرْبُوبٌ م: Created, made, newly-originated, nourished, regulated — five attributes affirming the spirit's creaturely status
key_terms.مُجَانِسَة: Mujanisa — being of the same genus/kind; explaining the natural affinity between spirits and wind

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the meaning of 'I breathed into him from My Spirit' in the Quran?
ai.summary: This hadith records Muhammad ibn Muslim's question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the Quranic phrase 'I breathed into him from My Spirit' (15:29). The Imam explains the etymology of 'Ruh' (Spirit) from 'Reeh' (wind), noting they share the same genus. The divine attribution 'My Spirit' is an honor, comparable to how God called the Ka'ba 'My house' and Ibrahim 'My Friend' — all of which remain created, newly-originated entities subject to God's nurturing and governance. This hadith addresses the theological concern of interpreting divine self-attribution without implying that the spirit is a part of God's essence, affirming strict divine transcendence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Abdul Hameed Al Taiy, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, 
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[15:29] and Blown into him from My Spirit.

How was this Blowing?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Spirit (Rooh) moves like the wind (Reeh), and rather it is named as ‘Rooh’ because it derived its name from the wind (Reeh), and rather it is extracted from the word ‘Reeh’, because the spirits (Arwaah) are the genus of the ‘Reeh’ (wind), and rather He<sup>azwj</sup> Supplemented it to His<sup>azwj</sup> Own Self, because He<sup>azwj</sup> Chose it over the rest of the spirits, just as He<sup>azwj</sup> Said for a House (Kabah) from the houses, ‘My house’, and for a Rasool<sup>as</sup> from the Rasools<sup>as</sup>, ‘My<sup>azwj</sup> Friend’, and the likes of that; and all of that is a Created being, newly occurred, Nourished, Regulated’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Qasin ibn ‘Urwa from ‘Abd al-Hamid al- Ta’i from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following. “I asked Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High,
‘I have blown My Spirit into it [15:29]’”

The Imam (a.s.) replied, “The spirit has motion like winds. It is called spirit (Ruh) because the word is a derivative of Rih (wind). This derivative is selected because the spirits are similar or are of the genus of the Rih (wind). He has given His own possessive case because He selected it from among the other spirits just as He has said about a House from among the houses ‘My house’ and to a messenger from among the messengers ‘My friend’ and so on. All such things are created, invented, newly produced and are cherished by the Lord.”
